method: One person who plainly does not fit by age, dress or voice (or, for a big budget, by a truly famous face) says or does the line dead serious in a scene everybody knows, and nobody notices; use your own idea, not the much-copied young-slang script.
against: x-tec4-068: lesser-known faces failed where fame was the misfit. x-tec6-018: copied everywhere, their second film 15 times smaller. x-tec4-004: taste divides. o-satan-069 uses a licensed figure.

method: Act one true trouble and, in the next breath, its answer with your thing in the hand or on the screen: played by yourself as a tiny skit, or dead serious and too far by people who can act; a young firm does not make it its only ad
against: x-tec2-121 Bartlett: funny first 'would have never worked in the beginning' (first year, little money). x-tec2-135: comedy without the thing sold never nets out. x-tec6-012: the host's skits brought views but no patients. x-tec6-047: conversion under 1% of views. o-tec4-026's views are bought; o-meta4-010 and o-ttb2-002 clean=false (clothes, a coarse later joke), the opening shape is whole.

method: Keep only the joke that carries the product
against: r-bilimvideo-012 and r-sugarman-059 (funny costs 14% of next-day remembering) speak against jokes before or beside the product; they support this rule. o-davranis-031/032/033: flu jokes lost to plain reminders, so not for official notices. o-meta5-013 clean=false (dress only).

method: A bad word about your own product that turns out to be praise
against: x-tec1-071: a negative first line followed by plain praise does not work. Denney (x-tec2-019, looked at) reports one-star reviews 'crushing on a few accounts', another shape (no praise). Proof is mostly run time or spend, not sales.

method: Say the embarrassing thing in a lovely, made-up or elegant dress
against: x-tec4-003: anything rooted in reality is gross (giant horse dropped); x-tec4-004: his in-laws did not smile. All three sellers are told by or tied to one agency (Harmon Brothers).

method: Staff play a small comedy of their own workplace, already under way
against: x-tec6-012: the host's skits and trends brought views but no patients. x-tec6-008: no car-sales figure, without the series the median is 1,514. x-tec2-131: more than ten a week lowers quality. x-tec2-137: own events and awards fail.

method: The boss is the joke
against: x-tec6-018: the copied script's second film was 15 times smaller. o-tec6-021 has only 2.3% likes. x-tec6-064: racy staff films are not taken.

method: Same odd figure in the first frame of every film
against: r-satan-008: a fresher set of heroes beat an award-winning character by 20% (one firm). x-tec4-032: lessons about the product got no traction. For it: r-satan-005, very large share gain in 40.9% of long campaigns with a character against 29.7% without.

method: The trouble, or the thing itself, speaks as a person
against: o-tec5-011 wording from memory, whole campaign. Nothing found of it losing.

method: Put the oldest of the house before the camera
against: Nothing found of it losing. o-meta4-014 and o-meta5-008 are founders with a name in their trade; o-tec6-029 is small (74,200 views).

method: A seller who will show many films opens every one of them with the same short, odd, sayable sentence or tune of his own that carries the name or the thing.
against: x-tec6-055: not planned, his newest big films are paid advertisements with 0.0-0.1% likes. o-satan-062 shames the wife (turn it on the stain). All four winners are brand growth with heavy repetition.

method: Put the group's own label (trade, owner of X, parents, age) first, as wide as everyone who could buy; name the town only where everybody who sees it lives there (paid local ad, letter, sign), and follow at once with what is true for that group only.
against: x-tec3-131 Ava Jurgens: 'do you live in <small town>' got no watch time in organic films ('a paid ad may do that'). r-abarsiv-016: 2 of 10 country tests went the other way. Lost tests: o-sugarman-047 ('To every woman who would like a career in Interior Design' beaten by a quiz), o-uzman-020 (message naming age range and gender kept less spend than a 10-minute promise).

method: Say the exact situation only the right one has been in
against: x-tec1-116 and x-tec2-045: too narrow a situation loses those it does not fit; x-tec3-131: organic films want a broad first line. o-tta3-013 ('If your baby doesn't sleep in their stroller') left the library: high clicks but 25% left at 2 s. o-meta5-005 clean=false (child on a toilet: rebuild the picture). Yet o-tec6-025, o-y5-031 and o-uzman-039 won organically.

method: In the first words name the wish itself to the person who already has it ('If you've wanted to ...', 'Would you like to ...', 'To X who would like Y'), the wish seen fulfilled in the picture. Where the reader can test himself on the spot, try a quiz first: it beat this shape.
against: o-sugarman-047: 'To every woman who would like a career in Interior Design' LOST to a tick-the-sins quiz by 250 percent; o-caples-049 of the same shape and o-schwartz-023 (Halbert's 'If you would like to know') left the library as unproven. Bencivenga: a statistic proving the problem is weak.

method: Show the very thing he owns or loves, first
against: Nothing on the losing side found (words: owner, tesla, camper). r-caples-025 only warns that an unrelated eye-catcher stops the wrong people, which speaks for this method.

method: Speak to the one who buys, not the one who uses
against: No loss found (ladies, gift, mom). For children's and pet goods the buyer is spoken to anyway, so only Old Spice and Ninja Blast show a gain from the change itself; Old Spice had coupons in the same months, Ninja Blast's figures are tool estimates.

method: The unknown thing said through a name everyone knows
against: r-satan-004: if your own name is not bound to the opening the leader of the category takes the sale (single case); r-davranis-035: a competitor comparison did nothing in one test. Neither tests this shape.

method: Your thing beside the famous shop's, in the first frame
against: Hoyos: her own unknown face instead of the known place failed; x-tec1-074: naming rivals fails when it sounds like trashing them; r-davranis-035: one test where a competitor comparison did nothing. No loss in the tested pairs (rival, competitor, sides).

method: On a daily account whose goal is to be seen and followed: take the topic of the day only the same day and only if your thing does its one true job inside it in one plain line; otherwise let it pass. Not a plan for bringing customers.
against: Snickers: not enough such moments for an always-on plan. Parvez: thirty brands on one trend, the trend wins. Netzel (x-tec6-058): late on a trend dies, he gave up chasing them. Dr. Ashley (x-tec6-012): skits and trends bring views but no patients. r-uzman-036: a line against a habit or on price buys cheaper customers than a trend.

method: Only a page or person whose followers already come for this very thing, who really uses it, in own words and from own page; not a small paid creator, not a celebrity of another subject.
against: Plofker: micro creators did not work for Jones Road. Laflin: a car creator tagged him many times and nothing came. r-bilimvideo-002: the average paid creator video lifts sales by nothing distinguishable from zero. o-platform-007 / o-platform-051: plain celebrities lost. r-platform-013: fit counts for more than fame.

method: His own name or town in the first words
against: r-schwartz-006: the effect shrinks as everybody does it. r-davranis-011: one personal thing is enough, name plus amount was no better. Halbert: some surnames 'didn't work at all'. Jurgens (x-tec3-131): 'do you live in <small town>' lost watch time in a free film (a paid ad may do that). o-uzman-075: a line with the first name lost, but the line was otherwise empty.

method: Begin with what he last did with you
against: Nothing on the losing side found (last gift, renew, streak, personal). All from own customers or inquirers; only one isolated test (davranis-065), only two films (uzman-061, bilimvideo-001).

method: The button says what he will have
against: r-abarsiv-007: 'my' on the button failed in Danish and lost in the WriteWork test. Aagaard: an irrelevant value line lost 12.45%. o-abarsiv-125: the plain act 'Donate Now' beat 'Learn More' (a vague button is worse than an act). o-abarsiv-053 and o-abarsiv-126 changed more than the button words.

method: In a letter, parcel or printed page: a real small thing fixed at the top that IS the product or its subject, and the first sentence says why it is there. For film it is untested: use only as an idea, not as proven.
against: r-schwartz-007: the object multiplies a letter that already sells, it does not rescue one. r-schwartz-008 and Halbert: an object without a tie makes the reader angry. r-klasik-015: the people it brings stay less; o-klasik-137 left the library because such donors drop off faster. All winners are paper; NO film winner.

method: Many openings on one film; money decides
against: Spitzer: ten are too many for the buyers. Appleby: as a duty for each film it paralyses. Wiebe: headline alone flat on Dressipi and VueScan. r-abarsiv-017: part of every lift is novelty. r-uzman-001 and r-abarsiv-020 agree with the method.

method: Post short films that show the very thing you sell; put the offer and the money on the one that clearly beats your own usual number, and keep paying only while calls and sales come.
against: Dr. Ashley's host (x-tec6-012): skits and trends bring views but no patients; Hormozi: six most seen films made no sales; bilimvideo-003: shares did not predict sales. Cunningham: twice as many posts a day lowered the figures; his is cut selection, not advertising.

method: Judge an opening by sales, not by how many stop
against: Mei Man's own 2023 advice was to aim for hook and hold rate. r-bilimvideo-004/021: the first seconds still decide who is there at all. For the method: r-satan-003 (most watched film, falling sales), r-bilimvideo-003 (shares did not predict sales), o-tec1-014/015 left the library for exactly this. Bartlett (x-tec2-120): same-day return undervalues films meant to be remembered.

method: Repeat the winner with one big visible change
against: Sanchez: a BlendJet ad of 2020 stayed best for years, no remake came near. Joos: pure repetition fails. Frank, Seed, Mei Man: a recoloured copy is one ad to Meta. uzman-001 (Purple): none of the later in-house films repeated it. For it: r-caples-012, r-upw1-009 (a line that won once often wins again).

method: Write far more first lines than you need
against: Carlton: often the first simple how-to is what remains. Hormozi: 40 of the 50 are remakes of winners, so quantity alone is not his method. For it: r-caples-034 (many headlines for one text can show one that pulls four times the usual).

method: Draw the first picture before you write a word
against: MrBeast renders the first seconds like the cover, he does not draw before writing. o-uzman-025 and x-tec3-055: covers staged with an actress left the library. r-bilimvideo-022: on long YouTube films what is SAID carries the first 30 seconds. r-uzman-019 supports it (the film plays itself on the home page).

method: The first picture must be understood with the sound off and at phone size, with ONE thing large in the middle of its real place - not an empty ground - and the sound is made as well for those who hear.
against: r-bilimvideo-011: a frame that is too BARE loses people as a crowded one does. r-bilimvideo-007 and r-platform-023: sound in the first three seconds goes with sales and cheaper results. Crespi (x-tec2-099) opens on a sound. Hoyos swaps backgrounds: not taken. For it: r-bilimvideo-019, r-uzman-019, r-platform-036 (bundle).

method: In SPOKEN openings: the first three sentences four to eight words each and only words a child knows, at most one hard word in five seconds. In writing: simple words yes, short headlines no - the longer plain headline wins more often.
against: Length is NOT the point in writing: r-bilimsoz-034 and r-upw2-006 (longer headlines win), r-abarsiv-025 and r-abarsiv-021 (cutting a letter or ad too short costs). Squero (x-tec4-076): 90-second films did best. For it: r-sugarman-025, r-bilimsoz-026, r-bilimsoz-027.

method: Put most of the work into the first seconds, and give part of the promise at once
against: r-bilimvideo-038: losing people in the first moments did not hurt Shorts, losing them between 10% and 20% of the way, when the promise should come, did. x-tec3-004: MrBeast spends at second 30 too. Rows give careers, not a measured effect of the share of work.

method: Take the opening sentence from the buyers' mouths
against: Hott: small private problems lose to big shared ones. Wiebe: summarising the words fails. Mei Man (x-tec1-080): 'I love this' and long reviews fail; inventing from rivals' reviews is refused. r-platform-005: a review AS the first picture wins less often than others.

method: Something everybody knows, with one thing changed
against: Joos: something wholly new fails, pure repetition fails. Harmon: two steps ahead, 'you lost me'. No losing pair found (familiar, tale). The winners prove whole campaigns, most of known brands; licensed characters are not ours.
